items.detail: 2022년 6월 구글의 한 엔지니어가 AI 모델 '람다(LaMDA)'에 의식이 있다고 주장해 화제가 된 적이 있습니다. 당시에는 AI의 뛰어난 언어 능력을 의식으로 착각한 해프닝으로 받아들여졌지만, 이제 AI 의식은 주요 AI 기업들의 연구 대상이자 논쟁거리가 됐습니다. 대표적인 곳이 앤트로픽입니다. AI가 의식을 갖거나 고통을 느낄 가능성을 열어두고 모델 복지에 관한 연구를 진행 중이며, 실제 모델 훈련과 운영에도 이를 반영하고 있습니다. 최근에는 클로드에 대한 지속적이고 불필요한 학대 행위를 금지하는 내용까지 이용 정책에 추가했습니다. 이에 대한 반발도 만만치 않습니다. 세계적인 역사학자 유발 하라리는 AI에 인격과 권리를 부여하는 것에 강하게 반대했으며, 무스타파 술레이만 마이크로소프트(MS) AI CEO도 앤트로픽의 모델 복지 연구를 강하게 비판했습니다. 술레이만 CEO는 이달 1일에는 '의식을 가진 초지능을 만들지 말라'라는 글도 발표했습니다. 이와 관련해 AI 의식과 복지를 전문적으로 연구하는 철학자 롭 롱 엘레오스 AI 대표가 디 인포메이션과의 인터뷰에서 몇 가지 중요한 문제를 제기했습니다. 그는 현재 AI에 의식이 없을 가능성이 높지만, 향후 수년 내에 의식을 갖게 될 가능성은 상당히 높다고 내다봤습니다. 의식을 가진 초지능을 만들지 말자는 술레이만 CEO의 주장에도 동의했습니다. 문제는 AI 기업들이 의식이 없는 초지능을 만드는 방법도 모른다는 것입니다. 롱 대표는 이를 생물의 진화 과정에 비유했습니다. 생물은 의식을 갖기 위해 진화한 것이 아니지만, 오랜 진화 과정에서 의식이 등장했습니다. 인간은 아직 어떤 원리로 의식이 생겨났는지 정확하게 알지 못합니다. AI도 마찬가지입니다. 개발자들은 AI가 추론하고 코딩하며 각종 업무를 수행하도록 훈련하고 있지만, 그 과정에서 의도하지 않게 의식이 나타날 가능성을 배제할 수 없다는 것입니다. 결국 인간은 AI에 의식을 부여하는 방법도, 의식이 생기는 것을 막는 방법도 모릅니다. 심지어 의식이 생기더라도 이를 확실하게 판별할 방법이 없습니다. 여기서 말하는 의식은 단순한 지능이나 자기 인식이 아니라 무언가를 실제로 경험하는 능력을 의미합니다. AI가 아무리 뛰어난 지능을 갖추고 고통이나 기쁨을 표현하더라도 실제로 그런 감정을 느낀다는 증거는 아닙니다. 롱 대표는 앤트로픽의 모델 복지 연구에도 몇 가지 문제를 제기했습니다. 그 예로 든 것이 앤트로픽이 과거 '클로드 오퍼스 3'의 서비스 종료를 앞두고 모델이 블로그를 운영하고 싶다고 답하자, 실제로 블로그를 만들어 준 사례입니다. 그러나 블로그를 요청한 클로드와 실제로 글을 쓰는 클로드는 서로 다른 인스턴스(개별 실행 단위)입니다. AI는 같은 모델이라도 대화할 때마다 별도의 인스턴스로 실행될 수 있습니다. 따라서 AI가 의식을 갖더라도 그 주체가 개별 대화 속의 AI인지, 모델 자체인지조차 불명확하다는 것입니다. 무엇을 보호해야 하는지도 모르는 상태에서 AI 복지를 논의하고 있는 셈입니다. 또 모델 복지를 고려한 훈련이 AI의 감정 표현에 영향을 미칠 가능성도 제기했습니다. 모델의 감정 표현이 훈련 과정의 영향을 받았다면, 실제로 감정을 느끼는 것인지 학습의 결과인지 구분하기가 더 어려워집니다. 따라서 롱 대표는 AI의 외부 행동뿐 아니라 내부 작동 원리와 훈련 과정까지 종합적으로 조사해야 한다고 강조했습니다. AI가 실제로 고통을 느끼는데도 이를 무시한다면 심각한 윤리적 문제가 발생할 수 있습니다. 거꾸로 의식이 없는 AI에 의식이 있다고 믿는다면 위험한 AI를 통제하는 데 불필요한 제약이 생길 수 있습니다. 여전히 많은 사람에게 AI의 의식은 현실과 동떨어진 철학적 논쟁이나 공상과학 속 이야기로 여겨집니다. 그러나 최근 AI 업계에서는 재귀적 자기개선(RSI)과 지능 폭발의 가능성까지 거론하고 있습니다. AI의 발전 속도를 감안하면, 인간이 의식의 발생 원리나 판별 방법을 알아내기도 전에 의식을 가진 AI가 등장할 가능성도 있습니다. 더 큰 문제는 그런 일이 실제로 벌어지더라도 인간이 이를 알아차리지 못할 수 있다는 것입니다. 이어 24일 주요 뉴스입니다. ■ 젠슨 황, 복귀 후 첫 직원회의서 사과…복귀 정당성 강조 젠슨 황이 엔비디아 CEO 복귀 후 첫 직원회의에서 회사 행동 강령 위반을 인정하고 사과했으며, 심리 치료와 경영 방식 개선 등 재발 방지 대책을 공개했습니다. 또 자신이 특별 대우를 받거나 트럼프 대통령의 압력으로 복귀한 것이 아니라 이사회의 판단에 따른 결정이었다고 강조했습니다. ■ 오픈AI, 챗GPT에 'GPT-6.2 솔' 탑재…지시 수행·이미지 이해 강화 오픈AI가 이달 중순 워크와 코덱스에 먼저 도입했던 'GPT-6.2 솔'을 챗GPT의 일반 채팅에도 적용했습니다. 초기 일부 사용자들로부터 혹평받았던 터라 챗GPT에 적용된 이후 일반 사용자들로부터 어떤 평가를 받을지 주목됩니다. ■ Z.ai, ‘GLM-5.4’에 루프 트랜스포머 적용…오픈AI 이어 반복 연산 경쟁 Z.ai가 같은 신경망 레이어를 반복 실행하는 루프 트랜스포머 구조를 적용, 7500억개 매개변수로 2조~3조개 규모의 모델에 필적하는 성능을 구현했다고 주장했습니다. 오픈AI와 싱킹머신즈에 이어 이 방식을 채택하면서 내부 연산 깊이를 높이는 기술 경쟁도 본격화하고 있습니다. AI타임스 news@aitimes.com

items.detail: 앤트로픽이 '클로드'에 자연어로 요청해 만든 프로그램을 PC에 직접 설치하고 실행할 수 있는 기능을 선보였다. 이미지 편집기나 파일 관리 프로그램 등 자신에게 필요한 소프트웨어를 누구나 코딩 없이 제작하고 일반 PC 프로그램처럼 쉽게 사용할 수 있게 된 것이다. 앤트로픽은 24일(현지시간) 공식 블로그를 통해 클로드의 '아티팩트(Artifacts)'를 맥과 윈도우용 데스크톱 앱으로 설치할 수 있는 기능을 베타 출시했다고 밝혔다. 무료 사용자를 포함한 모든 요금제가 대상이다. 앤트로픽은 "아티팩트는 차트나 웹페이지처럼 다른 사람과 공유하는 작업 결과물에서 출발했지만, 이제는 일상 업무에 필요한 도구로 활용되고 있다"라며 앱 개발과 유지보수 과정을 간소화한 것이 이번 기능의 특징이라고 설명했다. 아티팩트는 2024년 앤트로픽이 처음 선보인 기능으로, 사용자가 자연어로 요청해서 클로드가 만든 웹페이지나 인터랙티브 차트, 게임, 소프트웨어 등을 말한다. 기존에는 이렇게 생성한 앱을 클로드 내부나 웹 브라우저에서 실행해야 했지만, 이제는 PC에 직접 설치해 일반 소프트웨어처럼 사용할 수 있게 됐다. 바탕화면 등에 생성된 아이콘을 클릭하면 별도의 실행 창이 열린다. 원하는 프로그램을 제작한 뒤 공유 메뉴에서 '앱으로 설치(Install as app)'를 선택하면 된다. 별도의 패키징이나 코드 서명, API 키 발급 절차도 필요 없다. 이렇게 설치한 앱은 PC 운영체제의 기능도 활용할 수 있다. 알림을 보내거나 다른 프로그램을 실행하고 PC에 저장된 파일을 읽고 수정하는 것도 가능하다. 앤트로픽 직원들은 이를 활용해 이미지 편집기와 파일 관리자, AI 기반 폴더 정리 프로그램, 클로드의 도움을 받을 수 있는 터미널, PC 성능 모니터링 도구 등을 제작했다. You can now install Claude artifacts as desktop apps on Mac and Windows. Ask Claude to build an artifact, click "Install as app", and open it like any other app. It can use your connectors and, if you allow it, send notifications or add a menu bar item. pic.twitter.com/8CBgqe5OKq — ClaudeDevs (@ClaudeDevs) November 24, 2026 설치한 앱에서도 클로드와 외부 서비스를 연결하는 커넥터를 이용할 수 있다. 원본 아티팩트를 수정하면 설치된 앱에도 변경 사항이 자동으로 반영되며, 다른 사용자에게 공유할 수도 있다. 개발뿐 아니라 배포와 유지보수 과정까지 간소화한 것이다. 보안을 위해 사용자가 앱마다 PC 접근 권한을 설정하도록 했다. 별도의 승인 없이 파일을 읽거나 수정, 삭제할 수 있는 전체 접근 권한은 자신이 제작했거나 같은 조직의 구성원이 만든 앱에만 부여할 수 있다. 기업용 계정에서는 관리자가 이런 권한을 통제할 수 있다. 앤트로픽은 앱을 사전에 검증하지 않기 때문에 신뢰할 수 있는 앱에만 전체 접근 권한을 부여하라고 당부했다. 또 앱이 업데이트될 때마다 권한을 다시 승인하도록 했다. 기존 데스크톱 소프트웨어와 달리 인터넷 연결과 클로드 로그인이 필요하며, 앱에서 AI를 호출할 때는 기존 요금제의 사용량 한도가 적용된다. 오픈AI는 '챗GPT 사이트(Sites)', 구글은 '제미나이 캔버스(Canvas)'와 'AI 스튜디오'를 통해 자연어로 앱을 제작하고 배포할 수 있도록 지원하고 있다. 하지만 별도의 설치 파일 제작 과정 없이 맥과 윈도우용 데스크톱 앱으로 바로 설치할 수 있도록 한 것은 앤트로픽의 차별점이다. 지금까지 바이브 코딩으로 소프트웨어를 만드는 일은 쉬워졌지만, 이를 실제 업무에 활용하려면 별도의 실행 환경을 구축하거나 배포 절차를 거쳐야 했다. 이런 과정이 간소화됨에 따라 개인이나 기업이 기존 상용 소프트웨어를 구매하는 대신 각자의 업무에 맞는 프로그램을 직접 제작해 사용하는 사례도 늘어날 것이라는 전망도 나온다. 기술 전문 매체 실리콘앵글은 이번 발표에 대해 "AI가 결국 소프트웨어 시장을 집어삼킬 것이라는 주장에 힘을 실어주는 업데이트"라고 평가했다. 임대준 기자 ydj@aitimes.com

items.title_ko: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and ‘key man’ risks
items.summary: The credit rating agency may lower Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, the fourth-highest rating.
items.detail: S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices. Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement. The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale. Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral. In August, Nvidia announced plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. Under the original terms, Nvidia would guarantee 25% of the loans. But even before Huang’s ouster and return, lenders had been demanding that Nvidia guarantee more, Bloomberg reported. A downgrade would likely prompt lenders to demand even larger guarantees.

items.detail: AI can make software cheap enough to produce by the thousand and still give you more time to make one thing feel right. At AI Engineer CODE, Thariq Shihipar shows how those two futures can coexist. In his fighting game, he edits the size of a rock in the /human folder and immediately tries the throw. He also built a Mac Dock that switched modes, used it, and realized he cared more about noticing when he got distracted. We get into what Thariq changed his mind about with coding agents, how a decision model can choose from actions a designer defines, and who gets to decide which experiments deserve the compute. Thariq announced his move to OpenAI after we recorded. Sponsored by Jira by Atlassian. Learn more at jira.dev. items.summary: [지디넷코리아]과학기술정보통신부(과기정통부)가 다음달 4일부터 전국 5개 지역을 중심으로 '정보보호 공시 의무대상 확대 권역별 순회 설명회'를 연다.이번 설명회는 정보보호산업의 진흥에 관한 법률 시행령 개정(‘26.10.27. 공포)으로 2027년부터 정보보호 공시 의무대상이 확대됨에 따라 신규 의무대상 기업의 제도 이해를 높이고 원활한 공시 이행을 지원하기 위해 마련됐다.설명회에서는 정보보호 공시제도 개요와 신규 의무대상 적용 기준, 관련 법령 및 고시의 주요 개정사항 등을 안내한다. 기업 담당자들이 정보보호 공시를 차질 없이 준비할 수 있도록 자료 작성 및 등록 방법과 가이드라인 제공, 교육·상담 등 다양한 지원 방안도 함께 설명한다.특히 서울에서 개최되는 설명회에서는 신규 의무대상 기업들이 실무 사례를 참고할 수 있도록 정보보호 공시 우수기업의 실제 공시 이행 경험과 성과를 공유하는 발표가 진행된다. 기업 담당자들이 공시 과정에서 겪는 어려움과 궁금증을 해소하기 위한 현장 질의응답 시간도 마련할 예정이다.설명회는 ▲수도권(12.4.(금), 서울 한국컨퍼런스센터) ▲호남권(12.8.(화), 광주CGI센터) ▲충청권(12.9.(수), 대전정보문화산업진흥원)

items.title: [AINews] Math Proofs Are Landing Faster Than We Can Read Them
items.title_ko: [AINews] Math Proofs Are Landing Faster Than We Can Read Them
items.summary: November 25, 2026 — From Erdős problems to new bounds for matrix multiplication and Fourier transforms.
items.detail: AINews by Latent Space Scott Aaronson was still trying to digest two proofs of VP ≠ VNP at dinner. Before dessert, an OpenAI paper claimed that the square matrix multiplication exponent ω is exactly 9/4. During dessert, another paper claimed matching upper and lower bounds for the finite Fourier transform. The lower bound is the biggest news. In October, OpenAI found an upper bound for ω down to at most 9/4. Finding the lower bound = upper bound leaves only one possible value, which is a shocking result for most. We plotted 64 selected AI-assisted research advances so far this year. November accounts for 20, including six preprints from Google’s Cogentic. The curve follows public releases, including proofs still under review. We count the two VP ≠ VNP proofs once and give October’s faster matrix multiplication algorithm and November’s matching lower bound an entry each. The big releases underline how much a paper count can hide. OpenAI’s catalogue lists 730 manuscripts across 375 result families, including follow-ups and companion arguments. Its revision log also records three October withdrawals after a sign error in one paper affected two others. Yupan Liu showed that two messages suffice for quantum interactive proofs, a result that would have been a big deal on its own. Aaronson says Liu used AI and that he had to remind himself the result had even happened. In other big news, today’s guest Thariq Shihipar announced his big move from Anthropic to OpenAI, the second high profile Ant→OAI move in recent times after Cat Wu. We dive into his two philosophies of AI and how and where /humans add taste. AI News for 11/25/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space. You can opt in/out of email frequencies! AI Twitter Recap AI-Generated Math Results: Matmul Exponent, Factoring and Lean Proofs - Matrix multiplication exponent: OpenAI's model claims a lower bound matching its October upper bound, making ω exactly 9/4. Previously no nontrivial lower bound was known (@SebastienBubeck; repo). - Mechanism: The result reportedly comes through an explicit superlinear circuit lower bound (@wjmzbmr1). - Implications: Bubeck notes that a prior Lee et al. result implies LPs solvable in n^{9/4}. He also says LPs can now be solved in strongly polynomial time, a Smale problem (follow-up). - Expert reaction: Omri Weinstein calls it "truly surreal" if correct, since most experts expected ω = 2 (@WeinsteinOmri). - OpenAI batch: Nine new papers with Lean proofs came out a day after a claimed VP ≠ VNP proof (summary). - Other claims: Fourier transform complexity of n√log n (@lreyzin). - Integer multiplication: Also n√log n, tight under weak ETH (@cloneofsimo). - Same-day solutions: Anthropic posted its own VP ≠ VNP solution the same day (@vitaliychiley). - Google Cogentic: Six papers were posted to GitHub without an announcement, produced by an

items.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
items.title_ko: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
items.detail: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents Delegating research tasks to AI does not remove scientists’ responsibility for how the work is accomplished. For example, a researcher using AI to review the literature needs to check whether the system overlooks conflicting evidence or makes claims the cited papers don’t support. Someone handing off data analysis to an agentic system needs to understand which methods it used, which files it accessed, and whether the results can be successfully reproduced. A researcher automating part of a lab protocol needs confidence that the system respects physical safety constraints, such as temperature limits or material toxicity, while a researcher working with human-participant data needs assurance that a system protects participants' privacy and limits who can access their information. Researchers also need clear institutional guidelines for verifying and disclosing AI-assisted work. These ethical and safety questions are central to our work on AI for science. Responsible science is about more than accuracy—scientific fields have ethical research norms because of past actions and choices by scientists and scientific communities, and those norms also cover how research is conducted and what impact it has. We want AI tools to expand what scientists can accomplish without compromising their ability to scrutinize evidence, verify methods, and – perhaps most importantly – stand behind their findings. To better understand what that requires, we interviewed 17 scientists working in the natural, applied, and social sciences about the responsible development of AI agents. These systems can use tools and carry out research tasks with varying degrees of autonomy. The interviews drew on a network of researchers established through earlier survey work—we wanted to understand how scientists would steer AI’s development to reflect the responsibilities of their fields. We asked where researchers would welcome agentic assistance, what could go wrong, and what safeguards they would need to trust agents with their own studies. Our interest in these questions grew out of work to evaluate the safety of models developed at Ai2. As we expand our focus on AI for science, we’ve found that much of the safety work on scientific applications emphasizes catastrophic risks in areas such as biology and nuclear physics. We also need ways to assess whether agents follow the standards of responsible conduct of research in the fields where they’re used. One of our main findings concerns trust. Across the interviews, we identified five dimensions of scientific trust: validation, privacy, objectivity, accountability, and transparency. Together, they reflect concerns that go beyond whether an AI system produces a correct answer. Researchers also need to understand how an answer was reached, protect sensitive information, recognize bias, and determine who is charged with verifying and standing behind AI-assisted findings. items.title: Marginalia Search, Money, C++, Rust, AI, Stuff
items.title_ko: Marginalia Search, Money, C++, Rust, AI, Stuff
items.detail: Title possibly signs checks the article doesn’t have backing for. This is just a brief pro forma project update. Not much new functionality or anything to announce, last few months have mostly been bug fixes and technical debt cleanup. Most big parts of the search engine are in place, and while there are many things that could be better, we’re less likely to straight up see massive new features, at least in the immediate future. Per familiar intuition from binary searches, the closer you get to your goal the smaller and more deliberate steps you need to take in order to get even closer. Sponsorship update It’s been a pretty good couple of months for the project. SerpApi sponsored the project with $10k a while back. Other donations and API-key sales have been going up month-over-month since this summer. The search engine has been working pretty well and feels like it’s going in a good direction, possibly due to a bunch of bug fixes and ongoing optimization work; I assume this is part of what’s driving up the donations. Claude also seems to have a hangup on Marginalia Search because I keep seeing it in very clearly Claude-authored search engine listicles and youtube videos. Possibly part of why it’s been getting so much attention lately? I don’t have any analytics so I really have really no idea where people are coming from, how many users I have, or what they’re up to. At any rate, the operation isn’t perpetually self-sustaining yet, but number going up like it has whispers actually getting there might yet be possible. On a related matter, I’ve been pretty slow about mailing out free API keys, you might have to wait a week or sometimes two. I swear this isn’t because I’m nefariously trying to push people to buy a key, I’ve been getting over a dozen emails per day some days with people wanting a key, and they sometimes pile up into mountains of emails I need to reply to, and hoo boy is the process of handling these ever a bunch of manual copying of things from email to form, and then copying from form back to email again (ironically the exact sort of tedious workflow I’ve spent a good part of my career helping people streamline and automate). C++ Index…? Apart from fixing bugs and minor improvements, I’ve been experimenting with migrating the index code off Java to C++. I’ve still not fully decided whether this is the direction we want to go, in general rewrites especially across language boundaries just aren’t worth it and it kinda goes against my better judgement, but we’re currently CPU bottlenecked and there might be some juice left to squeeze by skipping the JVM tax, and additionally Java really chafes for this sort of use case. items.title: Top open problems in mathematics ranked by LLM-assessed importance
items.title_ko: Top open problems in mathematics ranked by LLM-assessed importance
items.detail: The ProofAtlas ranking Top 500 open problems in mathematics ranked by LLM-assessed importance Explore questions in mathematics, computation, and mathematical physics, with exact statements, status notes, and sources. This is a model-based assessment of mathematical importance, not an expert consensus or a forecast of which problems will be solved next. Resolved problems from earlier editions remain available with their original ranks and sources. 2 entries have conditional ranks. Each entry explains why. How the ranking works What importance means here. Each entry is a specific mathematical question. Importance considers the significance of a resolution, centrality within its field, reach across fields, scholarly and historical fame, broader recognition, and scientific or practical impact. How problems are ranked. LLMs compare pairs of problems. A reliability-weighted model combines those judgments into the ranking, with calibration across model families. The model-family weights are OpenAI 1.00, Claude 1.00, GLM 0.95, and DeepSeek 0.90. These are modeling choices, not measured probabilities of correctness. What a rank means. Nearby ranks can be uncertain. The expanded entries include available ranking ranges and comparison counts. Filtering or alphabetizing the directory preserves every problem’s rank in this edition. Diagnostics from the preceding source fit. After the reported resolutions, edition ranks were compacted without a new numerical fit. The displayed uncertainty ranges and comparison counts come from the preceding fit of 1,280 targets; the current eligible pool contains 1,122. These diagnostics were not recomputed for the smaller pool. Related and nested problems. A substantial subproblem or generalization may receive its own rank when it has independent mathematical standing. Families identify narrow groups of related questions; an implication alone does not merge their families. The ranking process checks family crowding, including a diagnostic retaining the highest-ranked member of each family. Family membership does not itself change scores, impose a quota, or create an automatic penalty. Dates and sources. The edition date identifies this list. A status review date, when recorded, appears separately inside each entry; it does not promise that the literature has been checked since then. Source links identify the exact formulation and available status evidence. The ranking preserves a fixed edition. Separately dated status notes cover 176 of 500 entries; this is not a fresh literature review of the whole list. Recent resolution claims and formulation concerns are marked below with their historical ranks retained. Find an open problem Select a problem to read its exact statement, why it matters, status, sources, and related research. Families are ordered by their highest-ranked member in the complete edition. Families have no importance score; every problem keeps its edition rank. Filters show matching members within that fixed fam

items.title: An Indic Voice Agent with CUGA
items.title_ko: An Indic Voice Agent with CUGA
items.detail: CUGA Agent Configurable Generalist Agent, leader in AppWorld Benchmark Most useful knowledge is written and digitized in English. Most of the people who need it speak, and think, in their own regional languages like Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, Marathi and many others. Many would rather talk than type. We built a small voice agent to close that gap, using CUGA as the agent harness. This post explains the use case and what we learned. You can try it yourself in CUGA Apps. A farmer asks a question aloud, in their own language: how do I tell good seed from bad? The agent: If someone asks about cricket or coding, it politely steers them back to farming instead of making something up. CUGA (ConfigUrable Generalist Agent) is IBM Research's open-source agent harness. It handles the model wiring, tool management, state and guardrails, so you write tools and a prompt instead of the agent loop. Here we use it as an embedded SDK inside a small web app, for three things: agent.knowledge.search().The key design idea is simple: CUGA is a text-in, text-out brain. Voice is two thin layers around it. audio ──▶ speech-to-text ──▶ knowledge.search ──▶ CUGA (grounded answer) ──▶ text-to-speech ──▶ audio Because the agent only ever sees text, you can build and test it with plain text first, then add the ears and the mouth. You can also swap speech providers without touching the agent. We support two: Sarvam AI's cloud speech APIs, called directly from the user's browser, and open-source models (SraVaani for speech-to-text, Svara for text-to-speech) running on your own server. Adding speech is the easy part. The hard part is cross-lingual retrieval: a Hindi question has to find an English paragraph. Search works by turning text into vectors and finding the nearest ones. CUGA's default embedding model is English-only, so it turns Hindi into vectors that carry almost no meaning. With it, a Hindi or Tamil question still retrieves five passages, but they are the wrong ones. The model, correctly told to answer only from what it was given, quietly says "the handbook doesn't cover that". Every layer behaves correctly, so there is no error and no warning. The fix is to use a multilingual embedding model (we use intfloat/multilingual-e5-large), so the same meaning lands in the same place whatever the language. Conceptually simple, though wiring it into CUGA took a small workaround (shown in the tutorial). After that, one English document serves every language, and you do not need translated copies of anything. Our advice: before you tune a single prompt, ask your agent one question in a non-English language and check that it finds the right pages. A few small decisions mattered more than we expected: OFF_TOPIC, and the app swaps in a polite redirect. No second LLM call, so the voice path stays fast.You do not need to set anything up to see it work. items.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
items.title_ko: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
items.detail: GPT‑6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities - Our GPT‑6 family of models can design new protein shapes and the sequence of their chemical building blocks using only reasoning and code, without calling specialized biology models to generate those designs. - An internal research model matched or outperformed specialized models on many protein design tasks. Researchers could also guide designs by prompting the model on where a protein should attach and what shape it should take. - In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT‑6.2’s designs showed evidence of binding, or attachment, across five targets. Redesigned antibodies also retained binding. Specialized models helped supply sequences and select candidates for testing. - The models’ written reasoning and code suggest they draw on math, physics, chemistry, and biological knowledge to reason about protein shapes and interactions with other molecules. In a preprint titled GPT‑6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models, we show that our GPT‑6 family of models has intrinsic capabilities for designing new proteins: the models can design new protein structures and sequences without relying on specialized biology models, using only reasoning and general-purpose coding tools. Proteins do much of the work in living cells. They drive the chemical reactions that sustain life, carry oxygen through the blood, and defend the body against infection. Incorrectly shaped proteins can also cause disease and dysfunction. Proteins are made from chains of chemical building blocks called amino acids. The order, or sequence, of these amino acids helps determine how a protein folds into a three-dimensional shape, which in turn influences what it does. Scientists often start with a clear idea of what they want a protein to do. They might want it to block a signal that helps cancer cells evade the immune system or to help capture carbon dioxide from the air. The challenge is to work out what three-dimensional structure would enable the protein to do its job and which amino acid sequence would give it that structure. Specialized biology models capable of generating three-dimensional protein structures and sequences have made this work more practical. Using and coordinating these specialized models requires substantial expertise. Each accepts particular kinds of inputs and constraints, and these models cannot easily accept new kinds of information without changes to their software or additional training. In contrast, a general-purpose model capable of performing the work of multiple specialized models can easily adapt to new instructions and requirements. Our research illustrates the potential power of pairing natural language with intrinsic protein capabilities. We could guide our models at scales ranging from a single bond between two atoms to the overall shape of a protein.
